rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening contrasts Noah’s idol-worshipping, disobedient people and Muhammad’s similarly hostile Arabs with jinn who readily accept the final, comprehensive revelation, rebuking the Arabs’ delay despite their shared language and kinship with Muhammad.
rows.anchor: ابتدئت , هذه بما كان من سهولة من سمع هذه الدعوة الخاتمة الجامعة من غير الجنس فضلا عن الموافقين في الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is for Muhammad to address his people with this news.
rows.anchor: قل } أي يا محمد لقومك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive wording gives prominence to the revelation, since the revealer of both messengers is one.
rows.anchor: المقصود تعظيم الموحى به , وأما الموحي إلى كل من الرسولين فواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad was secretly informed by the sole knower of the unseen through Gabriel; the Quran’s inimitability portends that he will have the most followers among prophets.
rows.anchor: أخبرت على وجه الخفاء ممن لا يعلم الغيب غيره في هذا القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn listened with exceptional attentiveness, receptivity, acceptance, and familiarity.
rows.anchor: بغاية الإصغاء والإقبال والتقبل والإلف استماعا هو الاستماع في الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn are living, rational bodies, predominantly fiery or airy, unlike humans, whose predominant nature is earthy.
rows.anchor: الذين هم في غاية الاستتار , وهم أجسام حية عاقلة خفيفة تغلب عليها النارية أو الهوائية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafar denotes a group of between three and ten.
rows.anchor: والنفر ما بين الثلاثة والعشرة

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi says the group consisted of nine jinn from Nasibin.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : وكانوا تسعة من جن نصيبين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported view counts seven jinn.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كانوا سبعة , وفي هذه العبارة دليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording indicates Muhammad neither saw the jinn nor recited to them; they happened to be present when he recited.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه العبارة دليل على أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم ما رآهم ولا قرأ عليهم , وإنما اتفق حضورهم عند قراءته

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says the well-known view identifies this listening with the jinn’s listening in al-Ahqaf.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : المشهور أنه هو , وقيل : هو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith evidence appears to indicate more than one encounter; one group came at Mecca from Nasibin and another at Nakhla from Nineveh.
rows.anchor: ويظهر من الحديث تعدد الواقعة , فمنها ما كان في المبدأ

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrimah says the jinn heard Surat al-Alaq.
rows.anchor: والسورة التي استمعوها قال عكرمة : العلق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the recited surah was al-Rahman.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة : العلق , وقيل : الرحمن

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: In a report in al-Sahih, the Prophet was missing one night; a caller from the jinn came, he went with them and recited Quran, then they showed him their tracks and fires.
rows.anchor: حديث عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه الذي في الصحيح ( أنهم فقدوه صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة من الليالي

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: In another report, Ibn Masud accompanied the Prophet to al-Hajun; the Prophet drew a boundary, recited to jinn hidden from Ibn Masud, and signaled him to remain seated.
rows.anchor: ومنها ما كان معه عبد الله رضي الله عنه فذهب معه إلى الحجون عند الشعب فخط عليه خطا , وقال : لا تجاوزه

rows.speaker: الأصبهاني
rows.claim: Al-Asbahani says they belonged to Banu al-Shaysaban, the most numerous jinn and the main body of Satan’s troops.
rows.anchor: قال الأصبهاني : وقيل : كانوا من بني الشيصبان وهم أكثر الجن عددا

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri says seven jinn came to Nakhla after the devils were pelted with meteors, believed, and told their people; later seventy from their people came to the Prophet and converted.
rows.anchor: وقال القشيري : لما رجمت الشياطين بالشهب فرق إبليس جنوده لعلم ذلك فأتى سبعة منهم بطن نخلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The listeners reported to those among the jinn who had not heard, or to their human allies, following the prophetic instruction to convey what one hears.
rows.anchor: فقالوا } أي فتسبب عن استماعهم أن قال من سمع منهم لمن لم يسمع , أو لمن كان يواخيهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed for the one who hears, understands, and conveys a saying as heard; no grading is stated here.
rows.anchor: لقوله النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( رحم الله امرأ سمع منا مقالة فوعاها فأداها كما سمعها )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inna is read with kasra because it begins a quoted statement after the verb of saying.
rows.anchor: بالكسر لأنه مبتدأ محكي بعد القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deliberately listened, turned their attention to the Quran, and were struck by it.
rows.anchor: حين تعمدنا الإصغاء وألقينا إليه فأهامنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call it speech exceptionally well ordered in itself and comprehensive of everything people need.
rows.anchor: كلاما هو في غاية الانتظام في نفسه والجمع لجميع ما نحتاج إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Quran ajab as a verbal noun intensifies its description: it is unprecedented and its cause is hidden.
rows.anchor: بالمصدر مبالغة في أمره فقالوا : { عجبا * } أي بديعا خارجا عن عادة أمثاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its arrangement, composition, and diction exceed divine books and human speech, while agreeing with scripture in calling to God, distinguishing good from evil, and summoning people to salvation.
rows.anchor: في جلالة النظم وإعجاز التركيب والوضع مع الموافقة لها في الدعوة إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn’s description shows their eloquence and command of rhetorical composition as well as their intellectual strength.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على قوتهم العلمية في فصاحتهم وكمالهم في علم الرسوم

rows.speaker: الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links this opening to the preceding surahs: after Quraysh’s obstinacy, the warning of al-Haqqah, its confirmation in al-Maarij, and consolation through Noah, the jinn’s response teaches the receptive that hearts are in God’s hands.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما تقدم ذكر حال كفار قريش في تعاميهم عن النظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account continues the jinn’s story from al-Ahqaf and connects it to their later report about the Arab unbelievers’ opposition to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: إلى قوله إخبارا عن تعريف الجن سائر أخوانهم بما شاهدوه من عنااد كفار العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran guides gently and with full clarity to truth and right conduct, which feels burdensome to desire-led souls, unlike easy error and foolishness.
rows.anchor: أي يبين غاية البيان مع الدعاء في لطف وهدى { إلى الرشد } أي الحق والصواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every jinn who listened believed at once; none held back or hesitated after hearing the Quran.
rows.anchor: كل من استمع منا لم يتخلف منا أحد ولا توقف بعد الاستماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They trusted the messenger who brought the Quran, resolving not to deny him or disobey him even slightly.
rows.anchor: أوقعنا الأمان لمبلغ القرآن أن نكذبه أو نخالفه أدنى مخالفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith must continue beyond the past act of belief; they therefore affirm that they will never associate anyone with God, the sole creator and benefactor.
rows.anchor: وكان الإيمان لا يفيد إلا مع الاستمرار , قالوا عاطفين على ما تقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call God their Lord because their existence and every subsequent favor come only from Him.
rows.anchor: الذي لا إحسان قائم بنا من الإيجاد ومابعده إلا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They exclude any created partner because no one shared in God’s acts, and the Quran’s evidence has made divine oneness clear.
rows.anchor: لأنه لم يشركه في شيء من مرنا أحد , وقد وضحت الدلائل على التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the listed clauses, Ibn Kathir, the Basrans, and Abu Jafar read the initial an clauses with kasra; Abu Jafar instead opens 72:3, 72:4, and 72:6, while Nafi and Abu Bakr agree with the kasra group except at 72:19. Ibn Amir, Hamza, al-Kisai, and Hafs open the rest, with the stated fa-in exception.
rows.anchor: وافقهم نافع وأبو بكر عن عاصم في غير ^ ( { وأنه لما قام } ) ^

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The open an clauses are connected to the revealed content, in the nominative; the fa clauses connect to the prepositional phrase in bihi by its syntactic position, not its surface form, or—by the Kufan view—directly to the pronoun.
rows.anchor: على أنه معطوف على محل الجار في ( به ) أي صدقناه وصدقنا أنه - لا على لفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taala means that God reaches an incomparable height and elevation; the greatness of His majesty makes His own transcendence greater still.
rows.anchor: تعالى } أي انتهى في العلو والارتفاع إلى حد لا يستطاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jadd here means greatness, authority, perfection, and absolute independence.
rows.anchor: جد } أي عظمة وسلطان وكمال غنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form ittakhadha identifies the deficiency at issue; it does not restrict the denial to a particular way of acquiring a spouse or child.
rows.anchor: عبر بصيغة الافتعال بيانا لموضع النقص لا تقيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A spouse implies a same-kind partner and conceptual composition; a child is a separated bodily part. Either entails composition and need, so God is exalted above both; creating without need would be futile.
rows.anchor: والصاحبة لا بد وأن تكون من نوع صاحبها , ومن له نوع فهو مركب تركيبا عقليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their collective term for their fool includes Iblis, the head of the jinn, and all followers ignorant of God, since knowledge bears the fruit of knowing Him.
rows.anchor: وهو الجنس فيتناول إبليس رأس الجنس تناولا أوليا , وكل من تبعه ممن لم يعرف الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shatat is speech far beyond right judgment, a transgression that exceeds proper bounds.
rows.anchor: قولا هو في بعده عن الصواب نفس البعد ومجاوزة الحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After warning that many will face judgment in disbelief, God consoles the Prophet, who grieves for people hostile to him, and promises to deal with their arrogance and delusion.
rows.anchor: هون أمرهم عليه وحقر شأنهم لديه بوعده بالكفاية بقوله مستأنفا منبها على أسباب الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells the Prophet to leave Him to deal with the man in whatever way the situation requires.
rows.anchor: ذرني } أي أتركني على أي حالة اتفقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man was created from nothing and formed through stages, originally possessing no wealth, children, or property.
rows.anchor: أوجدت من العدم وأنشأت في أطوار الخلقة , حال كونه { وحيدا * } لا مال له ولا ولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone created the man without a partner and remains firmly one in His oneness; the man failed to thank Him and instead committed shirk.
rows.anchor: وحال كوني أنا واحدا شديد الثبات في صفة الوحدانية لم يشاركني في صنعه أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the man’s wealth vast, growing, abundant, and available throughout his life; its provision came from God, not the man’s own power.
rows.anchor: مالا ممدودا * } أي مبسوطا واسعا ناميا كثيرا جدا عاما لجميع أوقات وجوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wealthy man intended here is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
rows.anchor: والمراد به كما يأتي الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says al-Walid owned camels, livestock, gardens, enslaved men and women, and other property between Mecca and Taif.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : كان له بين مكة والطائف إبل وحجور ونعم وجنان وعبيد وجوار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After abundant wealth, sons—especially male children—are a foremost worldly desire; their presence spared him travel and let him enjoy their company whenever he wished.
rows.anchor: أول ما يمتد إليه النفس بعد كثرة المال الولد , وكان أحب الولد الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuhud means the sons were constantly present, intelligent and capable, and prominent in gatherings, as though no one else attended.
rows.anchor: أي حضورا معه لغناه عن الأسفار بكثرة المال وانتشار الخدم وقوة الأعوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One of al-Walid’s sons, Khalid, later embraced Islam and became the sword of God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: منهم خالد الذي من الله بإسلامه , فكان سيف الله تعالى وسيف رسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gradually prepared al-Walid’s leadership and prestige, winning him both material possession and people’s hearts, prolonging his life, removing obstacles, and making elders seek his counsel.
rows.anchor: وطأت وبسطت وهيأت في الرئاسة بأن جمعت له إلى ملك الأعيان ملك المعاني التي منها القلوب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God gave him lands stretching from Yemen to Syria and completed his worldly fortune; he was called al-Wahid and Rayhanat Quraysh as the leading man of his clan.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : وسعت له ما بين اليمين إلى الشام فأكملت له من سعادة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamheed emphasizes the thorough extent of the preparation and comfort God gave him.
rows.anchor: وأكد ذلك بقوله : { تمهيدا * }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma marks the shocking distance between God’s immense favors and al-Walid’s later denial, after which he still expects an increase.
rows.anchor: مشيرا بأداة التراخي إلى استبعاد الزيادة له على حالته هذه من عدم الشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He expects further worldly or afterlife favor without offering gratitude, even while he denies God’s messenger.
rows.anchor: أزيد * } أي فيما آتيته من دنياه أو آخرته وهو يكذب رسولي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God decisively denies that he will receive more; if he persists, he will instead decline until his death, a prediction that demonstrates the prophethood.
rows.anchor: لا تكون له زيادة على ذلك أصلا , وأما النقصان فسيرى إن استمر على تكذيبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His innate, extreme obstinacy was directed specifically against God’s signs, which guide to divine oneness, rather than against deceptive arguments for shirk.
rows.anchor: لآياتنا } على مالها من العظمة خاصة لكونها هادية إلى الوحدانية

rows.speaker: الملوي
rows.claim: Al-Malawi defines obstinacy as deviation from the right path and crossing bounds persistently, including opposing truth while knowing it; it may arise from pride, a dry nature, bad character, or impaired reason.
rows.anchor: والعناد - كما قال الملوي : من كبر في النفس أو يبس في الطبع أو شرائة في الأخلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will subject him forcefully and inexorably to distress; the harsh punishment fits the hardness of his obstinacy.
rows.anchor: ألحقه بعنف وغلظة وقهر إلحاقا يغشاه ويحيط به بوعيد لا خلف فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suud can mean a steep, difficult ascent and here denotes severe ordeals and hardships.
rows.anchor: من الدواهي والأنكاد كأنه عقبة , فإن الصعود لغة العقبة شاق المصعد جدا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi reports from Abu Saeed that the Prophet described Suud as a mountain of fire climbed for seventy years before the climber falls; in another version, hands and feet melt on contact and are restored.
rows.anchor: وروي الترمذي عن أبي سعيد رضي الله عنه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه جبل من نار يتصعد فيه سبعين خريفا

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Suud is a slippery rock in Hell climbed with chains and iron blows; after forty years the climber falls from its summit and must climb again forever.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي : إنه صخرة ملساء في النار يكلف أن يصعدها بجذب من أمامه بسلاسل الحديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing his obstinacy and its punishment as Suud, the passage now details the afterlife recompense by naming Saqar.
rows.anchor: ولما انقضى بيان عناده فحصل التشوف لتفصيل جزائه في معاده , قال مبينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saqar is a fiery level whose intense heat attacks and melts the brain, answering the man’s own mental plotting to burn God’s friends.
rows.anchor: سقر * } أي الدركة النارية التي تفعل في الأدمغة من شدة حموها ما يجل عن الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will put him into Saqar under an inevitable threat that will come soon.
rows.anchor: فأدخله إياه وألوحه في الشدائد حرها وأذيب دماغه بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question ma adraka declares that Saqar’s reality exceeds human knowledge and inquiry, unless God informs someone.
rows.anchor: يعني أن علم هذا خارج عن طوق البشر لا يمكن أن يصل إليه أحد منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s question means, “What could make you know?” and signals the fire’s overwhelming severity.
rows.anchor: وما أدراك } أي أعلمك وإن اجتهدت في البحث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saqar leaves nothing in any condition: it continually destroys what it is allowed to destroy and alters the state of what it is allowed to punish, without fatigue.
rows.anchor: أي تترك على حالة من الحالات ولو كانت أقبح الحالات فضلا عما دونها , بل هي دائمة الإهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lawwaha describes intense heat that discolors and damages with blackness, blueness, flashing, convulsion, thirst, and similar effects.
rows.anchor: شديدة التغيير بالسواد والزرقة واللمع والاضطراب والتعطيش ونحوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arab usage, laha al-nar al-shay means that fire scorched and blackened something.
rows.anchor: تقول العرب : لاحت النار الشيء - إذا أحرقته وسودته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bashar can mean people, or their skin; bashara is singular skin and its plural is abshar.
rows.anchor: أي للناس أو لجلودهم , جمع بشرة وجمع البشر أبشار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nineteen are angels appointed over the fire; on the author’s proposed division, the upper layer has one and the remaining six have eighteen, three apiece.
rows.anchor: أي ملكا , لطبقة المؤمنين وهي العليا ملك واحد , وللست الباقية ثمانية عشر , لكل واحدة ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also suggests three angels per layer because one helper needs a second and the pair are strengthened by a third, or because the three denials concern God, His Book, and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: لأن الواحد يؤازر بثان , وهما يعززان بثالث , فلذا والله أعلم كانوا ثلاثة

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators hold that the nineteen are individual angels.
rows.anchor: وعلى الأول في كونهم أشخاطا بأعيانهم أكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: الآثار
rows.claim: Reports describe the keepers as huge, merciless angels with flashing eyes and hornlike teeth, flames from their mouths, and strength to hurl vast crowds into Hell.
rows.anchor: وجاء في الآثار أن أعينهم كالبرق الخاطف , وأنيابهم كالصياصي , يخرج لهب النار من أفواههم

rows.speaker: عمرو بن دينار
rows.claim: Amr ibn Dinar says a single keeper’s shove exceeds the combined strength of Rabi'a and Mudar.
rows.anchor: إن واحدا منهم يدفع بالدفعة الواحدةأكثر من ربيعة ومضر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One proposed symbolism matches nineteen to human powers: five external senses, five internal faculties, appetite and anger, and seven natural faculties.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن هذه العدة لمكافأة ما في الإنسان من القوى التي بها ينتظم قوامه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation makes nineteen comprehensive because nine is the end of units and ten the start of tens, combining the largest small number and smallest large one.
rows.anchor: وقيل : اختير هذا العدد لأن التسعة نهاية الآحاد , والعشر بداية العشرات , فصار مجموعهما

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Masud says reciting the basmala saves a person from the keepers because the basmala has nineteen letters, one for each angel.
rows.anchor: ويروى عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أن قراءة البسملة تنجي من خزنة النار لإإنها تسعة عشر حرفا

words: وَمَا جَعَلْنَآ أَصْحَٰبَ ٱلنَّارِ إِلَّا مَلَٰٓئِكَةًۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companions of the Fire are its keepers, not its human inmates; their angelic nature makes them powerful and prevents pity, weakness, or the inmates’ ability to overpower or rest with them.
rows.anchor: أصحاب النار } أي خزنتها { إلا ملائكتة } أي إنهم ليسوا من جنس المعذبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels are far stronger than human beings: a single angel’s cry can destroy an entire city, as happened to Thamud, and each keeper commands forces only God can count.
rows.anchor: بل الواحد منم يصيح صيحة واحدة فيهلك مدينة كاملة كما وقع لثمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The number is a trial because its wisdom is obscure and the scoffing disbeliever treats nineteen as too few, turning the count into an occasion for mockery and further unbelief.
rows.anchor: وكانت الحكمة في تعيين هذا العد غير ظاهر , وكان هذا العدد مما يستقله المتعنت فيزيده كفرا

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: Abu Jahl mocks the reported count, asking whether ten Quraysh men cannot overpower one keeper.
rows.anchor: أبو جهل , قال : ثكلتكم أمهاتكم , أسمع ابن أبي كبشة يقول كذا وأنتم أدلهم

rows.speaker: أبو الأشد بن أسيد بن كلدة الجمحي
rows.claim: Abu al-Ashadd boasts that he can handle seventeen angels himself while the others take two, in mockery of the warning.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو الأشد بن أسيد بن كلدة الجمحي - وكان شديد البطش : أنا أكفيكم سبعة عشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their taunting stems from denying resurrection and treating this description of its consequences as a target for obstinate challenge.
rows.anchor: وهذا كله على سبيل الاستهزاء , فإنهم مكذبون بالبعث الذي هذا من آثاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scripture’s people already know this number from their books, and hearing it confirms their certainty.
rows.anchor: وكان في علم أهل الكتاب أن هذه العدة عدتهم

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi says the number nineteen is written in the Torah and Gospel.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : مكتوب في التوراة والإنجيل أنهم تسعة عشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive wording “those given the Book” needs no named giver because the act of giving suffices and God is already understood as the giver.
rows.anchor: بناه للمفعول لأن مطلق الإيتاء كاف في ذلك من غير احتياج إلى تعيين المؤتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers grow in faith by affirming what they had not understood, especially when they see others tested by it; faith in such matters is greater.
rows.anchor: الإيمان بمثل ذلك يكون أعظم
